Given an owner requests `GET /api/usage`, When the response is built, Then it includes month-to-date spend in euros broken down by kind and by tender.

stories.summary: Stop a runaway AI bill with a per-account monthly spend ceiling
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Caps the one variable cost that can exceed a customer's entire subscription in an afternoon.

**Context**

`limits.ts` permits 400 drafts and 60 analyses per account per hour — well over €150/hour of model spend inside policy — and it is a rate limiter, not a budget. `monthlyUsage(accountId)` already aggregates spend per calendar month per account but nothing enforces against it. A prompt-injected 700k-char pack or a stuck retry loop currently has no financial ceiling at all.

**Notes**

Raised by the growth and monetisation analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given an account whose month-to-date spend is below its plan ceiling, When a model call is attempted, Then it proceeds and the ceiling check adds no user-visible latency.
Given an account at or above its ceiling, When any model call is attempted, Then `callModel` refuses before calling the API with a message naming the ceiling, the spend to date and the reset date.
Given an account crosses 50% or 80% of its ceiling, When an owner loads the app, Then a banner visible only to owners states the percentage used and offers to raise the plan.
Given a batch drafting run is in flight, When the ceiling is reached mid-run, Then the run stops cleanly with a stated reason, already-saved answers are retained, and no partial answer is written.

stories.summary: Cache the stable prefix of every drafting call
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Cuts cost per bid from roughly €12 to €4, which is what makes generous plan limits affordable.

**Context**

`grep -rn "cache_control" server/src/` returns nothing. Each draft call re-sends the system prompt, the full analysis blob, the company profile, the content of every verified evidence item and all people records at full rate — twelve times over a twelve-question tender. Volatile content (the question, prior answers) must move after the last breakpoint for the prefix to hit.

**Notes**

Raised by the growth and monetisation analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a drafting call, When the request is built, Then the system prompt, analysis blob, company profile, evidence content and people records form a stable prefix carrying `cache_control`, and the question plus prior answers follow it.
Given a second drafting call on the same tender within the cache TTL, When it completes, Then `usage.cache_read_input_tokens` is greater than zero and is recorded on the usage event.
Given a batch run over twelve questions, When it finishes, Then total metered cost is at least 50% below the same run measured before this change.
Given the evidence vault or company profile changes mid-tender, When the next draft runs, Then it uses the updated content and correctly re-creates the cache rather than citing stale evidence.

stories.summary: Meter drafting as bid credits and check the balance before a batch run
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Puts the meter where the cost and the value both are, while keeping qualification free so NO-GO stays cheap.

**Context**

Analysis costs roughly €1-2 and a NO-GO saves the customer three days, so charging for it would suppress the behaviour the product is best at. Drafting is where the tokens are: twelve calls per tender via `batch-draft.ts`, which runs outside the HTTP request. A credit must therefore be checked once in the route before the loop starts, not per call, or a run you meant to refuse spends half its money first.

**Notes**

Raised by the growth and monetisation analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a tender that has never been drafted, When any of `/draft-all`, `/draft` or `/draft-stream` is first called on it, Then exactly one bid credit is consumed and recorded against that tender with the actor and timestamp.
Given a tender that has already consumed a credit, When any further drafting, refining, critique, red-team, mock-evaluation or pack action runs on it, Then no additional credit is consumed.

Given an account with zero credits remaining, When drafting is requested, Then the request is refused with 402 before any model call, the message states the reset date and the price of an extra credit, and analysis and discovery remain fully available.
Given an owner buys a credit block, When payment succeeds, Then the balance increases immediately and the previously blocked drafting run can be started without re-import or re-analysis.

stories.summary: Right-size model and effort for every AI call site
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Cuts COGS on non-judgement calls by up to 80%, widening margin without touching output quality where it matters.

**Context**

`ai.ts:15` defaults every call to `claude-fable-5` at $10/$50 per MTok, and all but four call sites pass `effort: "high"`. Structured extraction — CV parsing at line 436, notice summarisation, rationale — does not need premium reasoning depth, while eligibility gates and drafting plainly do. Because `kind` is only analysis/draft/critique, cost per feature is currently unmeasurable, so this work must follow the euro ledger.

**Notes**

Raised by the growth and monetisation analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the usage meter records cost per call, When a per-call-site cost report is produced, Then each of the call sites in `ai.ts` is listed with its monthly cost and call volume.
Given a call site is classified as extraction rather than judgement, When it runs, Then it uses a cheaper model or lower effort, configurable per site rather than one global setting.
Given a model or effort change on a call site, When it is evaluated against saved fixtures, Then output quality is measured before and after and the change is reverted if quality drops.
Given the changes ship, When `usage_events` kinds are reviewed, Then each distinct capability is recorded under its own kind rather than every non-analysis, non-draft call landing in `critique`.

stories.summary: Offer approved answers from previous bids when drafting a similar question
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Gokul stops paying to rewrite the QA-approach answer he already approved twice.

**Context**

Drafting is strictly per-tender — no cross-tender answer retrieval exists in `drafting.ts` or `retrieval.ts`. Irish public tenders reuse the same scored questions constantly. He has not asked for this because he has not yet felt it, and he will feel it on about his third bid. It is the largest unclaimed time saving in the product.

**Notes**

Raised independently by the product manager and the SaaS acquisitions analyst, whose proposals are merged here.

The merged proposals were: "Offer approved answers from previous bids when drafting a similar question", "Build an organisation-wide answer library and retrieve it into every draft".

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a scored question and previously approved answers on other bids, When the user opens that question, Then the closest prior answers are offered with their tender, date and score context.
Given the user adopts a prior answer, When it is inserted, Then its provenance records that it was reused and from which bid.
Given a prior answer cites evidence that has since expired, When it is offered, Then the expiry is stated before it can be adopted.
Given no sufficiently similar prior answer exists, When the question opens, Then nothing is suggested rather than a weak match being offered.

Given an answer reaches `ready` status, when it is saved, then it is indexed into an organisation-scoped answer library with its question text, evaluation criterion, cited evidence and provenance class.

Given a new tender has a scored question, when drafting runs, then the three closest prior ready answers are retrieved and offered as reusable material, each shown with its tender, date and outcome where known.
Given a prior answer is reused, when the new draft is produced, then its provenance records the reuse and the citation chain from the original answer's evidence is carried forward.
Given a reused answer cited evidence that has since expired, when the draft is produced, then the expiry is surfaced as a blocker rather than silently reasserting a stale certificate.

stories.summary: Pool extracted tender requirement structures across tenants keyed on canonical notice
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Creates the product's first network effect — every new customer makes analysis instant for all existing ones.

**Context**

Analysis is per-tender and per-tenant today; two customers bidding the same notice each upload the same pack and each pay for the same model call. `008_canonical_key.sql` and `dedupe.ts` already identify one opportunity across eTenders and TED, so the join key exists. The extracted requirement structure is Tenderly's own work product, distinct from the buyer's document bytes.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS acquisitions analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given tenant A has analysed notice X, when tenant B ingests the same canonical notice, then B receives the gates, evaluation criteria, weightings, scored questions and checklist without uploading a pack or triggering a model call.

Given a pooled structure is used, when B's workspace renders it, then it is labelled as derived from a shared requirement record with its extraction date, and B can force a fresh analysis of its own pack.

Given a pooled structure exists, when B views it, then no document bytes, answers, evidence, company profile or identity belonging to A are reachable, proven by a test in the style of `tenant-isolation.test.ts`.
Given a customer opts out of pooling in settings, when they analyse a pack, then their extraction is not contributed to the pool and they still consume from it.

stories.summary: Ship a real sample tender pack every new account can analyse in one click
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Delivers the aha inside 15 minutes of signup with no eTenders login and no upload, for about €1.50 per trial.

**Context**

A new prospect without an eTenders account and without a pack in hand currently sees an empty board and never reaches a GO/NO-GO verdict. The aha is the eligibility gate that refuses a tender with a quoted reason before three days are wasted — that needs a real pack with real gates, weightings and scored questions. One anonymised pack, shipped as a fixture, reaches it on click.

**Notes**

Raised independently by the growth and monetisation analyst and the SaaS marketing analyst, whose proposals are merged here.

The merged proposals were: "Ship a real sample tender pack every new account can analyse in one click", "Ship a one-click sample tender so a new workspace produces value with no pack".

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a newly registered account, When they open the discovery board, Then a clearly labelled sample tender is offered with a one-click analyse action.
Given they analyse the sample, When it completes, Then they see eligibility gates with quoted evidence, evaluation criteria with weightings, scored questions and a GO/REVIEW/NO-GO verdict.
Given the sample is analysed, When the account's usage is metered, Then the cost is recorded against the trial ceiling like any other analysis.
Given the sample exists in an account, When real tenders are imported, Then the sample is visually distinct from them and can be dismissed permanently.
Given an empty new workspace, When I choose "Try a sample tender", Then a sample notice and pack are imported into my own workspace and full analysis runs.
Given the sample analysis, When I read it, Then it shows at least one gate held at Review and at least one `[INPUT NEEDED: …]` placeholder, so the refusal is visible on the first run.
Given the sample tender, When I request the final pack, Then it is refused with the blocker list, and the draft pack downloads.
Given a sample tender exists in my workspace, When I view it, Then it is labelled as a sample and can be removed in one action.

stories.summary: Show the answer-reuse rate on every bid so the library's compounding value is visible
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Makes the switching cost felt month over month, which is the core retention mechanic.

**Context**

Every accepted answer, verified evidence item and parsed CV makes the next bid cheaper — bid one comes back mostly `[INPUT NEEDED]`, bid six mostly citable. That asset compounds invisibly today, so a customer under cost pressure sees a subscription rather than something they would be deleting. Provenance and citations are already recorded per answer, so the inputs exist.

**Notes**

Raised by the growth and monetisation analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a tender with drafted answers, When the user opens it, Then they see how many answers drew on prior bids or vault evidence, how many need new input, and the reuse percentage.
Given an account with more than one completed bid, When an owner opens the portfolio, Then the reuse rate is shown as a trend across bids in order.
Given a bid's first draft, When reuse is calculated, Then it counts only verified, in-date evidence and previously accepted answers, never unverified or expired items.
Given an account's first ever bid, When it is drafted, Then the reuse panel states plainly that this is the first bid and that later bids will reuse its answers.

stories.summary: Add mandatory MFA and SAML single sign-on for larger buyers
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Lifts the addressable customer size past the smallest SMEs by clearing the security questionnaire that blocks every larger deal.

**Context**

`server/src/auth.ts` exports only `signToken`, `requireAuth`, `accountId`, `userId` and `actorEmail`; a 12-hour JWT cannot be revoked, and a forgotten password is unrecoverable. `TENANCY.md` notes that `attachMembership` re-reads the membership row per request, so access removal works — but the session itself does not. Any bidder large enough to have an IT policy fails this at first contact.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS acquisitions analyst.

Password reset and session revocation were split out of this proposal into their own story, because they are needed before the first paying customer and this is not.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given an owner enables mandatory MFA for the organisation, when any member signs in, then a second factor is required and a member without one is guided to enrol before reaching any tender data.

Given an organisation configures SAML SSO, when a member signs in through the identity provider, then their membership and role are resolved without a Tenderly password and de-provisioning at the IdP removes access on their next request.

stories.summary: Split index.ts and db.ts into feature modules and retire the in-memory mirror
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Removes the largest drag on delivery speed and the clearest technical-debt finding in diligence.

**Context**

`server/src/index.ts` is 2,336 lines and 119KB carrying 91 routes with handler logic inline; `server/src/db.ts` is 2,329 lines and 108KB holding every query plus a complete `memory.*` mirror of all 32 tables so the app can run without a database. That mirror doubles the cost of every schema change permanently, in exchange for a demo convenience that a seeded ephemeral Postgres delivers better.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS acquisitions analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the route modules are extracted, when the API boots, then every one of the 91 existing routes resolves at its current path with its current auth, role and rate-limit behaviour, proven by the existing suite passing unchanged.
Given the data layer is split by domain, when a new column is added, then it is implemented once against Postgres with no parallel in-memory branch to maintain.

Given local development previously relied on the in-memory store, when a developer runs the documented command, then an ephemeral Postgres is started and seeded, and the developer experience is no worse.
Given `no DATABASE_URL` in a production environment, when the API boots, then it refuses to start rather than silently serving a store that loses everything on restart.

stories.summary: Rewrite ARCHITECTURE.md and GAPS.md against the code and gate them in CI
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Protects every unverifiable claim made in diligence by making the verifiable ones true.

**Context**

Both documents are dated 2026-08-19 and describe a 974-line frontend, an OpenAI `gpt-5.6` dependency, absent tenancy, absent provenance, absent GDPR machinery and three test files. The code now runs Anthropic `claude-fable-5` via a forced tool call with Zod validation, full organisation and membership tenancy, a provenance ledger, GDPR export and erasure, and 59 test files. The honesty of these documents is a genuine asset and it is currently rotting.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS acquisitions analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the architecture document, when it is read against the repository, then the module table, the route count, the table count, the model provider and the test inventory all match what is actually there.

Given the gap analysis, when a gap has been closed, then it is marked closed with the migration or module that closed it, and gaps still open — billing, email, outcomes, object storage, auth lifecycle — are restated with today's date.
Given a pull request changes the migration count or adds a route, when CI runs, then it fails unless the counts stated in the architecture document are updated in the same change.
Given a reader new to the repository, when they follow the documents, then nothing they are told contradicts the code they then open.

stories.summary: Add password reset and session revocation
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Removes a support failure that would land on a solo founder and a box every IT reviewer ticks.

**Context**

The only auth routes are `/api/auth/login` and `/api/auth/register`, and the sign-in form in `components/TenderlyApp.tsx:3878` has no reset link. `server/src/set-password.ts` exists for invitation acceptance, so the token and hashing machinery is already present.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS marketing analyst.

Session revocation is included here rather than with MFA and SSO: a 12-hour JWT currently lives out its life with no way to revoke it, so a reset that leaves old sessions valid is not a reset.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given I have forgotten my password, When I request a reset with my email, Then the same confirmation is shown whether or not the account exists.
Given a valid reset link, When I set a new password of at least ten characters, Then I can sign in with it and the old password no longer works.
Given a reset link, When it is older than its expiry or has already been used, Then it is refused and no password is changed.
Given a reset completes, When I view the audit log, Then the reset is recorded with its time and the account it affected.
Given a user signs out, When they next present the old token, Then it is refused, and the revocation is recorded in the audit log.
Given a password reset completes, When it is applied, Then every existing session for that user is invalidated.

stories.summary: Build a crawlable marketing and docs surface outside the single-page app
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Creates the only inbound channel a solo operator can afford, which today does not exist at all.

**Context**

`web-static/index.html` is one page with one meta description, no Open Graph tags, no canonical and no sitemap; `public/` holds only `favicon.svg`; and `netlify.toml` redirects `/*` to the app shell, so there are no crawlable URLs. The app cannot be the website.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS marketing analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the site is deployed, When a crawler requests a marketing or docs URL, Then it receives server-rendered HTML with a unique title, description, canonical and Open Graph tags.
Given the site is deployed, When I request `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml`, Then both exist and the sitemap lists every marketing and docs page.
Given a marketing or docs URL, When it is requested, Then it is not swallowed by the SPA catch-all redirect.
Given the docs surface, When I read it, Then it documents the evidence rules, the pack lock and the no-AI mode in the words the product itself uses.

stories.summary: Publish security, privacy, DPA and sub-processor pages as real URLs
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Turns already-good compliance work into a sales asset a prospect's IT contact can be sent.

**Context**

`docs/DATA_PROCESSING.md` is a genuinely strong buyer-facing document — named sub-processors with locations and honest "not yet in use" markers, retention periods with their env overrides, self-service export and deletion — but it lives only in the repo, and the SPA catch-all means `/privacy` serves the app shell. No DPA exists in any form, and no transfer position covers the US AI sub-processor.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS marketing analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given I am not signed in, When I open the security, privacy, sub-processor and DPA URLs, Then each returns its own page, not the application shell.
Given the sub-processor page, When I read it, Then every entry names what it processes, where, and whether it is in use, matching what the deployed system actually calls.
Given a prospect asks for a DPA, When they open the DPA URL, Then a signable agreement is available covering the US transfer for AI processing.
Given the security page, When I read it, Then it states plainly what does not exist yet — no MFA, no SSO, no external certification — rather than omitting it.

stories.summary: Reconcile the AI sub-processor disclosure across README, ARCHITECTURE and DATA_PROCESSING
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Removes an inaccuracy in a disclosure document, found by exactly the reviewer most worth impressing.

**Context**

`README.md:24,31` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:103` say OpenAI with `gpt-5.6`; `SETUP_CHECKLIST.md:61` says `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `claude-fable-5`; `docs/DATA_PROCESSING.md` publishes Anthropic, United States, in use, and states customer data is never used for training. A buyer reading the public repo and the sub-processor page finds a contradiction about who processes their confidential bid material.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS marketing analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the deployed API, When I check which model vendor it calls, Then one vendor is established as the truth with evidence from the code and the deploy config.
Given that truth, When I read the README, ARCHITECTURE and DATA_PROCESSING, Then all three name the same vendor and model, and the diagrams match.
Given a vendor is named as in use, When I read its entry, Then the stated location and training position match that vendor's actual commercial terms.
Given the docs are corrected, When a reviewer compares any two of them, Then no statement about data processing conflicts.

stories.summary: Settle on one domain, own it, and align CORS with the links the product sends
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Stops invitation links pointing at an origin the API distrusts, and stops the trust pitch being undercut by a *.netlify.app URL.

**Context**

`render.yaml:24` and `server/src/index.ts:149` allow-list `tenderly.netlify.app`; `server/src/invitations.ts:77` defaults invitation links to `gettenderly.netlify.app`; `README.md:89,100` and `DEPLOYMENT_CHECKLIST.md` say `tenderly.netlify.app`. Three documents and two code paths disagree about the product's own address.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS marketing analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a custom domain is configured, When I open the product, Then it serves from that domain over HTTPS and the old host redirects to it.
Given an invitation is created, When I inspect the link, Then its origin is on the API's CORS allow-list and the invitation flow completes from that origin.
Given the repo, When I grep for the product URL, Then every occurrence in code, deploy config and docs names the same host.
Given the domain changes, When I check the deploy config, Then the allowed origins come from configuration rather than a hardcoded default.

stories.summary: Publish the prompt versions and the tests that pin the evidence rules
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Converts the differentiator from a claim into something a sceptic can verify, which no competitor can copy cheaply.

**Context**

Every prompt carries a version constant (`ANALYSIS_PROMPT_VERSION = "analysis-2026-08-24.2"` and seven more), the version is stored on each analysis and provenance record, and the file comments state that tests assert the REVIEW-not-FAIL and `[INPUT NEEDED]` clauses so that deleting one fails the build. None of this is visible to a buyer.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS marketing analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the docs surface, When I open the evidence-rules page, Then it shows the current prompt version strings and the exact rule clauses they contain.
Given that page, When I follow the link to the tests, Then I reach the assertions that fail if a rule clause is removed.
Given a prompt version changes, When the docs are built, Then the published version string matches the code or the build fails.
Given an analysis in the product, When I inspect it, Then the prompt version that produced it is shown to the user, not only stored.

stories.summary: Retrieve login-gated tender packs through the customer's own eTenders session
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Unlocks the only hard part of the product for every notice, converting a thin notice summary into full analysis without manual work.

**Context**

TLY-168 measured 28 of 28 documents across 10 live notices as portal-gated, so `notice-summary.ts` honestly reports `packUnread` and four unassessed areas. `etenders.ts` can only fetch public documents and flags HTML content-type as "requires portal access". Every competitor faces the same wall; solving it is category ownership, not a chore.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS acquisitions analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a customer has installed the browser helper and is signed in to eTenders, when the 05:00 job puts a matched notice on the board, then the helper fetches that notice's documents using the customer's own session and uploads them to the tender as `source` documents.
Given documents arrive via the helper, when extraction completes, then full analysis runs automatically and `packUnread` becomes false with no human action.

Given the helper cannot authenticate, when it reports back, then the tender keeps its notice-level summary and the customer is told which notices need a manual pack upload, never that analysis is complete.
Given a document is retrieved, when it is stored, then its provenance records that it came from the customer's own authenticated session and not from a Tenderly crawl.

stories.summary: Add UK Find a Tender and Contracts Finder as ingestion sources
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Multiplies addressable market roughly thirtyfold for a few weeks of work, because Ireland alone caps out around €1–2m ARR.

**Context**

`DATA_SOURCES.md` assessed three Irish-focused sources and `sources/ted.ts` already proves the pattern for a keyed-free versioned API. CPV is the shared identifier and `cpv.ts` already resolves the hierarchy, so matching, scoring and ingestion need no new logic. Irish public procurement is ~€18–20bn a year against UK's several hundred billion.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS acquisitions analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a company profile carries CPV codes, when the discovery job runs, then UK Find a Tender and Contracts Finder are queried alongside eTenders and TED and their notices are scored by the same `scoreNotice` path.
Given the same opportunity appears on a UK source and on TED, when discovery returns, then `dedupe.ts` merges them into one row with both sources listed, as it already does for eTenders and TED.
Given a UK source is unavailable, when the job runs, then `Promise.allSettled` keeps the other sources' results and the failure is recorded as an ingestion run with an alarm.

Given a UK notice is ingested, when it is displayed, then its jurisdiction and its source are stated, and any licence attribution the source requires travels with the row as `award_history` already does.

stories.summary: Match bidders into consortia using the gate each partner would close
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Adds a two-sided network effect and per-match expansion revenue on top of subscription, and is the hardest item for a competitor to copy.

**Context**

`Decision = "PARTNER"` is declared in `packages/shared/src/index.ts:13` and nothing implements partnering. `eligibility.ts` already produces `DeterministicGate` with `required` and `held` as numbers, so the system knows precisely which gate fails and by how much. An SME failing a €6.5m turnover test alone clears it in a consortium, and today Tenderly tells it to walk away.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS acquisitions analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a tender's eligibility rolls up to REVIEW or FAIL on a capacity or turnover gate, when the recommendation is computed, then the shortfall is stated as a number and a partnering option is offered rather than only a NO-GO.

Given a customer opts into the partner network, when another customer on the same canonical notice has a profile that closes the failing gate, then each is offered an introduction naming only the gate closed and no other commercial detail.

Given both parties accept, when the introduction is made, then a consortium record links the two accounts for that tender and the eligibility roll-up is recomputed against the combined capacity with each figure attributed to its member.
Given a customer has not opted in, when matching runs, then their profile is never offered to anyone and their tenders never surface a partner.

stories.summary: Emit a signed AI-use declaration into the submission pack
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Converts the provenance ledger from an internal feature into a regulatory differentiator buyers actively prefer.

**Context**

`answer_provenance` records ai-generated, ai-assisted or human per answer with evidence citations; `no-ai-mode`, `AiUsePolicy` acknowledgement and `attestation.ts` all exist. None of it leaves the building — `pack.ts` puts the evidence register in `_Tenderly_Internal/`. Buyers increasingly ask bidders to disclose AI use, and Tenderly is the only tool that can answer truthfully at sentence level.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS acquisitions analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a final pack is built, when the ZIP is assembled, then it contains a buyer-facing AI-use declaration stating, per scored question, whether the text was human-written, AI-assisted or AI-generated with human review.
Given the declaration is generated, when it is signed by the attesting person, then it carries their name, role, timestamp and a digest over the answers it describes, so a later edit invalidates it.
Given no-AI mode was on for the tender, when the declaration is produced, then it states that no model was used for any drafted content and the ledger corroborates it.
Given a buyer receives the declaration, when they check any claim in it, then every statement is traceable to an `answer_provenance` row and none is generated prose.

stories.summary: Publish price-to-win and incumbent intelligence from award history
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Raises willingness to pay by answering the question a director actually asks, using data no competitor has assembled.

**Context**

`awardIntelligence(authority, cpv)` already computes award count, median, min, max and top three suppliers with a CPV-division fallback, and `companyWonBefore` and `knownBuyersFor` already feed scoring. The output is a panel; it does not yet tell anyone what to bid. `award_history` also holds `no_of_bids_received` and `no_of_smes_bids_received`, which are unexploited.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS acquisitions analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a tender names a buyer and a CPV with at least five awards in history, when the customer opens qualification, then they see the median award value, the ratio of awarded to estimated value, the typical bidder count and the SME share of bidders, each with its sample size.

Given an incumbent has won three or more of that buyer's awards under that CPV, when intelligence renders, then the incumbent is named with its win count and the customer is told it faces an entrenched supplier.
Given history is thin or absent, when intelligence renders, then it says so plainly and shows no figure, rather than falling back to a national average presented as local truth.
Given any figure derived from the OGP dataset is displayed, when the panel renders, then the CC-BY-4.0 attribution stored on the rows is shown with it.

stories.summary: Support framework and DPS lifecycles including mini-competitions
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Converts one-off bid work into multi-year recurring revenue with a naturally high renewal rate.

**Context**

`types.ts` and the analysis schema treat a tender as a single competition with one deadline, and `ai.ts` prompts encode that a framework is not a closed procurement. But there is no object representing a framework a customer has been admitted to, nor the stream of call-offs and mini-competitions that follow. In Irish IT procurement, framework membership is where the multi-year revenue is, and the reuse potential across call-offs is enormous.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS acquisitions analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a customer is admitted to a framework or DPS, when they record it, then a framework record holds the awarding body, lots, CPV scope, term and renewal date.

Given a framework exists, when a mini-competition or call-off under it is discovered or imported, then it is linked to the framework and pre-populated with the eligibility already established at framework stage.
Given a call-off is drafted, when retrieval runs, then answers from prior call-offs on the same framework are preferred over unrelated tenders.
Given a framework term is within 90 days of expiry, when the reminder job runs, then the owner is notified that re-qualification is due.

stories.summary: Launch a buyer-side bid assurance portal for contracting authorities
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Opens a second revenue side on the same data and dataset, which is how an Irish SME tool reaches a €25m valuation.

**Context**

Everything needed to serve the buy side already exists on the sell side: `answer_provenance` per sentence, `attestation.ts`, `AiUsePolicy`, `award_history`, and the eligibility engine that maps a stated requirement to evidence. Contracting authorities have the mirror-image problem — knowing which bids were AI-drafted and whether claimed evidence is real — and no tool answers it. This also makes Tenderly the system of record for both ends of one transaction.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS acquisitions analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a buyer organisation is onboarded, when a bidder submits with a Tenderly AI-use declaration, then the buyer can verify the declaration's digest against the ledger that produced it and see which sections were model-written.

Given a buyer uploads their own draft tender documents, when they request a review, then they are told which of their stated gates are unevidenceable by a typical SME and which criteria carry weightings that do not sum, citing their own text.
Given a buyer account, when it reads anything, then it can reach only bids submitted to it and never a bidder's vault, profile, unsubmitted drafts or other competitions, proven by isolation tests.
Given no bidder has consented to buyer-side verification, when a buyer looks up a bid, then nothing is disclosed and the buyer is told consent is required.

stories.summary: Publish award-history pages for every buyer and CPV code
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Compounding, near-zero-marginal-cost acquisition built from data already being crawled.

**Context**

OGP award history is already ingested and used in discovery scoring via `knownBuyersFor`. That same data answers the exact queries an SME director types in the week before he decides to bid — who won HSE IT contracts last year, what the awards in his CPV are worth. Publishing it costs nothing beyond rendering and creates the only acquisition asset that appreciates.

**Notes**

Raised by the growth and monetisation analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given an ingested award record, When the public pages are generated, Then a buyer page and a CPV page exist listing awards with winner, value and date, and both are indexable with no login.
Given a visitor on a public page, When they reach the end, Then they are offered current open tenders in that CPV behind a signup.
Given new award data is ingested, When the generation job runs, Then affected pages are regenerated within 24 hours.
Given award data contains personal data, When pages are generated, Then only organisation-level information is published, never named individuals.

stories.summary: Publish an Irish Public Procurement SME Index from award_history
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Turns already-loaded licensed data into original citable research — the cheapest authority a solo operator can build.

**Context**

`docs/DATA_SOURCES.md` confirms the OGP dataset covers every published Irish competition from 2013, quarterly, CC-BY-4.0, with awarded value, suppliers, bids received and SME bids received; `server/src/db.ts` already computes median/min/max award value and top suppliers per authority and CPV. Nobody publishes an SME's real odds — average bidders per competition and SME share of awards — and the licence permits it with attribution already stored per row.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS marketing analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the award data is loaded, When the index is generated, Then it reports SME share of awards and median award value by contracting authority and by CPV division, with the number of competitions behind each figure.
Given a figure derived from the dataset, When it is displayed or published, Then the CC-BY-4.0 attribution travels with it.
Given a cell with too few competitions to be meaningful, When the index is rendered, Then it is suppressed rather than published as a percentage.
Given the index pages, When a crawler requests them, Then each has its own crawlable URL, title and description.

stories.summary: Introduce a tender-source adapter so a second portal is configuration, not a rewrite
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

The prerequisite for every market beyond Ireland; without it UK and EU expansion is a fork.

**Context**

`server/src/etenders.ts:4-5` hardcodes `ETENDERS_HOSTS` as the whole procurement allow-list, `START_URL` is a fixed eTenders search URL, error strings name eTenders, and `extractStructuredFields` scans 33 literal eTenders labels while `parseSearchHtml` reads fixed table positions. `docs/DATA_SOURCES.md` rates this stability Low with no drift alarm.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS marketing analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a source adapter interface, When a new portal is registered, Then it supplies its own host allow-list, search entry point and field map without changes to shared import code.
Given any adapter, When it fetches, Then HTTPS-only, redirect re-validation, the request timeout and the size caps are enforced per adapter with no path that bypasses them.
Given a URL from an unregistered host, When a user tries to import it, Then it is refused with a message naming the portals that are supported.
Given an adapter's field map drifts, When ingestion health runs, Then an alarm fires naming the source and the fields that came back empty.

stories.summary: Carry contract value as amount plus currency code instead of a euro-formatted string
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

A GBP tender rendering as euro would destroy credibility on the first UK demo.

**Context**

`server/src/eligibility.ts:80`, `components/TenderlyApp.tsx:723` and `:2283` all format with `Intl.NumberFormat("en-IE", { currency: "EUR" })`; `server/src/pack.ts:110-111` sets `pptx.lang = "en-IE"`; the discovery filter is labelled "Contract value range (EUR)"; and demo value is the literal string `"€49,000"`. Currency is assumed rather than carried.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS marketing analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a notice from any source, When its value is ingested, Then the amount and its ISO currency code are stored separately and no formatted string is persisted as the value.
Given a stored value, When it is displayed, Then it renders in its own currency, never converted or relabelled.
Given a value-range filter, When I set it, Then the filter states which currency it applies to and compares only like currencies.
Given a notice that states no value, When it is displayed, Then it says so rather than showing zero.

stories.summary: Add a UK Standard Selection Questionnaire set alongside the ESPD declarations
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

The declaration set is the gate on UK usability; without it the product cannot complete a UK bid.

**Context**

`server/src/declarations.ts` implements ESPD Part III (grounds for exclusion) and Part IV (selection criteria), which is the EU-wide instrument and ports across member states essentially unchanged. The UK does not use ESPD — it uses a Standard Selection Questionnaire and centrally held supplier information — so it needs a parallel set, reusing the same affirm-once-and-reuse machinery.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS marketing analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a workspace set to the UK, When I open declarations, Then I see the UK selection questions and not the ESPD parts.
Given a workspace set to Ireland or another EU market, When I open declarations, Then I see the ESPD parts unchanged.
Given an answer that requires explanation, When I affirm without supplying detail, Then it is refused and names what is missing.
Given declarations affirmed in one jurisdiction, When I switch jurisdiction, Then the original affirmations are preserved and not silently reused for the other set.

stories.summary: Wire TED into discovery, handling language-keyed fields and CPV arrays
stories.description:
**Why this matters**

Proves the source abstraction against a stable credential-free API and opens above-threshold EU coverage.

**Context**

`docs/DATA_SOURCES.md` verified `POST https://api.ted.europa.eu/v3/notices/search` needs no key for published notices and returns CPV in the listing, which eTenders does not. It also names the trap: `notice-title` and `buyer-name` are language-keyed objects like `{"eng": ["…"]}` and `classification-cpv` is an array, so an ingest assuming strings silently stores `[object Object]`.

**Notes**

Raised by the SaaS marketing analyst.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given a TED notice, When it is ingested, Then title and buyer are read from the language-keyed object and no field stores `[object Object]`.
Given a TED notice with several CPV codes, When it is ingested, Then every code is normalised against the committed CPV list and matched with its ancestors.
Given a notice available in several languages, When it is displayed, Then one language is chosen deterministically and the notice states which.
Given both eTenders and TED publish the same competition, When discovery runs, Then it appears once, deduplicated on the shared reference.
